Second-opinion maintainer review of gastownhall/beads PR 5132 (fix(doctor): run graph integrity checks without CGO). A Claude reviewer recommends APPROVE, reasoning: dolt.New is server-mode-only and already linked into nocgo builds via cmd/bd/store_factory_nocgo.go, so the //go:build cgo stubs in cmd/bd/doctor were shadowing code the binary already contained; the PR deletes the stubs and untags the real files, deletions-only, no internal/storage changes; CGO_ENABLED=0 go build/vet pass on head and after trial-merge with main. Your job: try to REFUTE the approve. Use gh pr view/diff 5132 --repo gastownhall/beads and the local checkout at bd-main (upstream/main fetched). Focus: does any deleted nocgo stub have behavior a caller depends on (skip semantics, error strings, exit codes)? Does untagging pull any transitively-cgo dependency into nocgo doctor builds? Any hidden build-tag interaction with gms_pure_go? End with VERDICT: CONCUR or REFUTE plus one-paragraph rationale.

I’m using the repository’s Beads and delegation-metadata skills because this is upstream PR maintenance. I’ll run the read-only maintainer preflight, inspect every deleted stub and its callers/build constraints, then independently test the no-CGO and `gms_pure_go` build graph. I’ll make no GitHub changes.

The Beads skill’s required tracker lookup is blocked by this session’s read-only filesystem: embedded Dolt cannot open its lock file. I’m continuing with the review because all substantive actions are read-only; I won’t alter bead state or the PR.

GitHub CLI access is blocked by the environment’s network restriction, so the requested live `gh` preflight/view/diff cannot complete. I’m checking the locally fetched PR refs and upstream history next; if PR 5132’s head is present, I can still review the exact commit and compare it with the fetched `upstream/main`.

The exact PR head is available at the existing isolated worktree (`f1c9ddef6`). The first adversarial signal is test coverage: the PR deletes all explicit `!cgo` migration tests, while the real validation/maintenance test files remain `//go:build cgo`; therefore the claimed no-CGO behavior is build-checked but not behavior-tested. I’m now tracing whether that gap hides a real semantic regression.

I found the exact no-CGO `gms_pure_go` binary produced by the first review. I’m using it with auto-start disabled and test-mode’s port firewall, so it cannot start a server or touch production data, to test the key refutation hypothesis: whether an unavailable database becomes a false-green validation exit.

VERDICT: REFUTE — No transitive-CGO or `gms_pure_go` problem exists, but the deleted stubs carry meaningful failure semantics. In a no-CGO build with an unreachable Dolt server, the four `--check=validate` stubs previously returned warnings, forcing exit 1. Their real implementations instead return `StatusOK` with “N/A (no database/unable to open database)”; combined with the already-permissive cross-table check, `validateOverallOK` can now report success despite running zero integrity checks. Existing CGO parity does not negate this new no-CGO false-green regression. Preserve non-success semantics for unavailable checks and add a no-CGO exit-code test before approval.
